abstract: The European Union opened a formal investigation into Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, citing concerns that the U.K.-based bottling business may have abused its dominance in the EU.
content:
By Edith Hancock

The European Union opened a formal investigation into Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, citing concerns that the U.K.-based bottling business may have abused its dominance in the EU.

The European Commission, the EU's executive arm, said Monday that it is concerned the company- which is one of the biggest European bottlers under the Coca-Cola Company's brands --may have abused its dominance in the wholesale supply of soft drinks to supermarkets and retailers in the EU.

The commission said it will look into whether the company restricted cross-border trade of carbonated soft drinks, including by making wholesale price reductions conditional based on them not being exported to other countries in the bloc, practising targeted product differentiation across the region and denying some customers the chance to negotiate procurement for multiple countries.

CCEP did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: EU Probes Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, Citing Antitrust Concerns
